messages:
alex: pushed a follow-up to PR #8427 — addressed the allocator race and added a unit test. split into two commits (fix + test). link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8427 :tada:
maria: nice. quick skim — do the new tests rely on the internal timing spoof? trying to avoid flakiness in CI.
cheng: i looked at the diff. test is sensible but one comment: the retry backoff now uses 8ms default, could we make it configurable for tests? otherwise lgtm.
simon: alex do you mind adding a short note in the PR body about the test determinism and how it avoids hanging in long-running CI nodes? saved me time earlier.
alex: good call. updated the PR body with how the test injects a fake timer and added a short screenshot of local run. i also ran `./scripts/test-runtime --filter allocator_test` locally twice.
devops-bot: CI queued for runtime PR #8427 — run id: 993412 (expected ~12m).
maria: i'll run a quick local stress (`./scripts/stress-run --cases=allocator`) after lunch and report back.
cheng: ptal when you get a sec @maria @simon — mostly minor nits, but asking for a recheck because i changed the locking order in the second commit.
simon: will do a pass this afternoon. if CI is green and no regressions from stress tests, we can pick a canary slot tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks all — pinging again when CI finishes or if anyone sees flaky behavior.
devops-bot: CI passed for runtime PR #8427 — run id: 993412. status: success. artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/993412
maria: CI green and my local stress passed 3x without flake. sending LGTM on the lock-order change.
simon: LGTM as well. removing WIP label and scheduling canary for 08:30 UTC tomorrow.
alex: awesome, thanks everyone!
